text: I'd say test everything, we've run in the last four years over 600 experiments on the streaks, so every other day. We've actually set up really good infrastructure for copy testing.
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Lenny asks Jackson about the key lessons and insights from Duolingo's journey of building and iterating on their streaks feature. Jackson is explaining Duolingo's philosophy of constantly testing and experimenting, sharing specific examples of how small changes like copy adjustments can have massive impact. He emphasizes the importance of testing rather than debating ideas internally, demonstrating how a simple change from 'continue' to 'commit to my goal' became a huge win for user engagement.
text_ko: 전부 다 테스트해 보라고 말하고 싶어요. 지난 4년 동안 스트릭스(streaks) 관련해서 600건이 넘는 실험을 했어요. 거의 하루 걸러 한 번 꼴이에요. 실제로 카피 테스트(copy testing)를 위한 인프라도 정말 잘 갖춰놨아요.
text_zh: 我会说，什么都要测。过去四年里，我们在 streaks 功能（streaks）上做了 600 多个实验，差不多每两天就跑一个。其实我们已经把文案测试的基础设施（copy testing）搭得挺完善的。
text_es: Yo diría que prueben todo. En los últimos cuatro años hemos hecho más de 600 experimentos sobre los streaks (streaks), así que casi uno cada dos días. De hecho, hemos montado una infraestructura muy buena para hacer pruebas de copy (copy testing).
key_sentence: test everything, we've run in the last four years over 600 experiments on the streaks
original_text: I'd say test everything, we've run in the last four years over 600 experiments on the streaks, so every other day. We've actually set up really good infrastructure for copy testing. We used to say continue, our standard CTA is continue, and we changed that to commit to my goal, and it was a massive win.

vocabulary.definition: The fundamental facilities and systems that support the operation of an organization or service, including physical structures and organizational frameworks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, infrastructure refers to the underlying systems that enable operations, such as IT networks, software platforms, and logistical frameworks essential for efficient functioning.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with physical structures, in a business context, it can also imply the organizational processes and technologies that support strategic goals.

vocabulary.definition: Systematic tests or trials conducted to discover or validate information, often involving the manipulation of variables to observe outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, experiments are crucial for product development and market research, allowing teams to test hypotheses and refine offerings based on data-driven insights.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a methodical approach to testing ideas, often implying a willingness to take risks and learn from failures.

vocabulary.definition: The act of evaluating a product, process, or concept to determine its functionality, performance, or quality, often through controlled conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, testing is essential for quality assurance, user experience optimization, and ensuring that products meet market needs before launch.
vocabulary.nuance: While it implies a systematic approach, testing can also carry a connotation of trial and error, highlighting the importance of experimentation in innovation.

text: And this is not just the subjective retention PM talking, I think this is our biggest feature, with the exception of the lessons. Streaks are a great engagement hack.
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Lenny asks Jackson to explain the impact that the streaks feature has had on Duolingo's success and growth. Jackson is emphasizing that while streaks can be a powerful engagement mechanic for any app, they only work when layered on top of a product that users genuinely want to use. He's making the point that streaks are an 'engagement hack' - a retention tool that amplifies user engagement - but cannot substitute for core product value.
text_ko: 이건 단지 제가 리텐션 담당 PM(retention PM)이라서 하는 주관적인 말이 아니라, 레슨(lessons)을 제외하면 이게 우리 제품에서 가장 큰 기능이라고 생각해요. 스트릭스(Streaks)는 참여를 끌어올리는 효과적인 기법(engagement hack)이에요.
key_sentence: Streaks are a great engagement hack for user retention at the core.
original_text: And this is not just the subjective retention PM talking, I think this is our biggest feature, with the exception of the lessons. Streaks are a great engagement hack. I'm of the opinion that any team, any app out there can introduce a streak, and if you figure it out, it probably works to retain users, but at the core, you have to have an app that people want to use.

vocabulary.definition: Retention refers to the ability to keep customers or employees engaged and continuing to use a product or service over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, retention is a critical metric that indicates customer loyalty and satisfaction, often measured through customer retention rates or employee turnover rates.
vocabulary.nuance: While retention generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a need for improvement if retention rates are low, suggesting potential issues with customer satisfaction or product value.

vocabulary.definition: Engagement refers to the level of interaction, involvement, and emotional connection that users or employees have with a product, service, or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, engagement is often used to assess how actively users participate with a platform or how committed employees are to their work, impacting overall productivity and satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: Engagement can be both positive and negative; high engagement often indicates a strong connection, while low engagement may suggest apathy or dissatisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: A feature is a distinctive attribute or aspect of a product or service that provides value to users and differentiates it from competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, features are often highlighted in marketing strategies to attract users and can be critical in product development discussions to ensure alignment with customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'feature' typically has a neutral connotation, it can imply complexity or unnecessary additions if overused or poorly implemented.

text: We have right now over 9 million users with a year plus streak. So, 9 million of our users have used Duolingo every year, almost every day, for well over a year. Which is pretty...
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Jackson is providing concrete statistics to demonstrate the massive scale and impact of Duolingo's streaks feature. He's explaining that 9 million users have maintained streaks for over a year, meaning they've used the app almost daily for that entire period. He uses the analogy of imagining all these users as a large city to help contextualize the impressive scale of user engagement and retention that the streaks feature has achieved.
text_ko: 지금 1년 이상 연속 사용 기록(스트릭, streak)을 가진 사용자가 900만 명이 넘어요. 다시 말해 900만 명의 사용자가 1년 넘게 거의 매일 듀오링고를 사용해 왔어요. 그건 꽤 인상적이에요.
text_zh: 我们现在有超过900万用户保持一年以上的连胜（streak）。也就是说，有900万用户一年多来几乎每天都在用 Duolingo。挺厉害的。
text_es: Ahora mismo tenemos más de 9 millones de usuarios que llevan una racha de más de un año (streak). Es decir, 9 millones de nuestros usuarios han usado Duolingo casi todos los días durante más de un año. Lo cual es bastante...
key_sentence: Over 9 million users have a year plus streak, like a large city.
original_text: We have right now over 9 million users with a year plus streak. So, 9 million of our users have used Duolingo every year, almost every day, for well over a year. Which is pretty... I don't know, I like to imagine things in terms of like, okay, well, if you put all these people in a city, or in a place, where would it be? I'm like, ah, it's like a very large city, 9 million people.

text: What Duolingo really focuses on is, how do we help users build habits around language learning? Getting user come back the next day is the biggest problem to solve.
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Jackson is explaining Duolingo's core philosophy and approach to user retention. He's describing how Duolingo views the challenge of language learning - that the biggest obstacle isn't the learning content itself, but getting users to return consistently to build lasting habits. He emphasizes that from a growth perspective, streaks have objectively been their most effective tool for driving daily active users, which aligns with their broader growth strategy of focusing on retention rather than just acquisition.
text_ko: 듀오링고가 진짜로 신경 쓰는 건 이용자들이 언어 학습을 습관화(habit formation)하도록 어떻게 도와줄지예요. 사용자가 다음 날에도 돌아오게 하는 게 가장 큰 문제예요.
text_zh: Duolingo真正关心的是，怎么帮用户养成学语言的习惯。让用户第二天还会回来，才是我们要解决的最大问题。
text_es: Lo que Duolingo realmente se pregunta es: ¿cómo ayudamos a los usuarios a convertir el aprendizaje de idiomas en un hábito? Conseguir que vuelvan al día siguiente es el mayor reto.
key_sentence: Getting user come back the next day is the biggest problem to solve.
original_text: What Duolingo really focuses on is, how do we help users build habits around language learning? Getting user come back the next day is the biggest problem to solve. If you look at the numbers, I think pretty objectively has been our biggest growth lever for driving DAUs, and also say a lot of it's just related to how we think about growth at Duolingo.

vocabulary.definition: To build habits means to establish consistent behaviors or routines that become automatic over time. This often involves repeated actions that reinforce a desired behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and tech, building habits is crucial for user engagement, as companies strive to create products that encourage regular usage and integration into daily life.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase 'build habits' implies a long-term commitment to behavior change, often requiring strategies that promote gradual adoption rather than immediate results.

text: We actually tested, hey, what if we make it even easier to extend your streak? And so, we actually tested, hey, if you do one exercise, just one exercise in a lesson will extend your streak.
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Jackson is sharing a specific example of an experiment that failed, where Duolingo tested making it even easier to maintain a streak by requiring just one exercise instead of a full lesson. This was following their successful experiment of simplifying streaks from XP-based to lesson-based. He explains that this experiment taught them about the importance of having a meaningful 'unit of measure' - the core action that users need to complete. Making the requirement too easy actually captured less engaged users and provided no benefit to daily active users.
text_ko: 사실 저희가 '스트릭(streak)을 더 쉽게 이어가게 하면 어떨까?' 하고 실제로 테스트해봤어요. 한 레슨에서 연습 문제 하나만 해도 스트릭(streak)이 이어지도록요.
text_zh: 我们其实做了个测试，想看看要是把延长打卡天数(streak)弄得更容易会怎样。于是我们就试了：只要在一节课里做哪怕一个练习，打卡天数(streak)就会续上。
text_es: De hecho lo probamos: ¿y si lo hacemos aún más fácil para alargar la racha? Resultó que con hacer un solo ejercicio en una lección ya basta para que la racha se extienda.
key_sentence: if you do one exercise, just one exercise in a lesson will extend your streak.
original_text: We actually tested, hey, what if we make it even easier to extend your streak? And so, we actually tested, hey, if you do one exercise, just one exercise in a lesson will extend your streak. What we realized when we ran this experiment is DAUs moved not one bit. And what we were doing by... And if we go back to unit of measure, we had dumbed down the unit of measure that we were basing our streak around.

vocabulary.definition: To increase the length, duration, or scope of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, extending often refers to expanding product features, service offerings, or customer engagement strategies to enhance user experience.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'extend' generally has a positive connotation of growth and improvement, it can also imply overreach if not managed properly.

text: One of the fun ones that we did, and it's honestly as much about process as it is about the feature itself, was we have a feature called streak goal, and it is...
speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
context: Jackson is describing the development of Duolingo's 'streak goal' feature, which allows users to commit to reaching specific streak milestones. He's emphasizing how innovations often seem obvious in hindsight but were novel when first conceived. This feature emerged from focusing on the critical 0-7 day user experience, where they discovered that once users reach a 7-day streak, loss aversion kicks in and retention dramatically improves. The streak goal feature helps guide users toward that crucial milestone.
text_ko: 저희가 했던 재밌는 것들 중 하나였는데요, 솔직히 기능 자체만큼이나 그 과정을 중시한 프로젝트였어요. '연속 달성 목표(streak goal)'라는 기능이 있고, 그건...
text_zh: 我们做过的一个挺有意思的事儿，老实说这事儿跟功能本身比起来，更像是在讲流程。我们有个叫“连胜目标”(streak goal)的功能，它是……
text_es: Una de las cosas más divertidas que hicimos, y la verdad es que tiene tanto que ver con el proceso como con la funcionalidad (feature) en sí, fue implementar una funcionalidad llamada objetivo de rachas (streak goal), y es...
key_sentence: it's honestly as much about process as it is about the feature itself
original_text: One of the fun ones that we did, and it's honestly as much about process as it is about the feature itself, was we have a feature called streak goal, and it is... Again, so much of this stuff seems so obvious in retrospect, but it was really novel at the time. We had this idea of like, hey, maybe we'll just goal users to hitting a certain streak length.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end or result.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'process' often refers to workflows or methodologies that guide project execution and operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'process' implies a systematic approach, it can sometimes suggest rigidity; in creative contexts, flexibility may be preferred.

vocabulary.definition: A distinctive attribute or aspect of a product or service that provides value to users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, 'feature' often describes specific functionalities within software or applications that enhance user experience and engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'feature' can imply a selling point, but overemphasis on features without addressing user needs may lead to product failures.
